limitations: Fixed finite population N>=2, 0<mu<1, positive fixed confidence radius
Near-consensus initial states; Gaussian independent noise on interacting pair only
Bounded derivatives through order three of log utility
Only finite-time weak convergence; no interchange with microscopic stationarity
Invariant density requires integrability of the stated utility power
scientific_integrity: The convergence theorem is proved for fixed N, near-consensus initial states and smooth positive opinion-only utility on finite accelerated horizons. The invariant law belongs to the limiting diffusion only. The exact centered stationary variance requires constant utility and unrestricted pair interactions; it is used as a fast-mode limit in the nonlinear argument. No claim of convergence of microscopic stationary laws, uniform-time approximation or simultaneous population limit. Finite rational tests verify algebra, not infinite-time or weak-convergence assertions.
title: The finite-population Gibbs exponent for noisy utility-weighted opinion averaging
